title: 3  Models and Systems
text:
Finally, before reaching the primary topic of this site we have one last topic I would like to explain. In mathematics models have a formal definition but it isn’t really necessary to use it here. The important thing is that a model uses assumptions and works on a given universe.
For example, consider the band Ghost. In 2013 they did a cover of a song If You Have Ghost. In the lyrics one of the lines reads almost like an implication: “If you have ghosts, you have everything”. Normally you could read this meaning metaphorically but if we change the model through definitions we can change the meaning.
Let ghosts mean specifically the band and let everything be defined as music. This will be our definition for the model. Then consider that if you listen to Ghost’s cover that you have ghosts. Thus in our model by modus ponens we have everything or in other words we have music.
For a more formal version of this quasi-proof:

Proof.  
Definitions for the model, followed by modus ponens:
\[
\begin{array}{l}
\text{ghosts} := \text{the band Ghost} \\
\text{everything} := \text{music} \\[1em]
\text{ghosts} \implies \text{everything} \\
\text{ghosts} \\
\hline
\therefore \text{everything}
\end{array}
\]
